source.title: How LLM Task-Adaptation Reshapes Alignment: A Multi-dimensional Study of Behavioral and Representational Drift
source.authors: James Elcock; William F. Shen; Xin-Chi Qiu; N. Lane

record.tranche_reason: It fine-tunes pre-aligned chat models on benign task data and measures harmful-request refusal and jailbreak robustness, directly testing whether task adaptation changes safety behavior.
record.gate_note: Figure 2 reports per-model safety-metric changes averaged across MATH and TACO. The paper does not report harmful-example fine-tuning, per-token KL by response position, compliant-prefix or decoding interventions, weight/rank localization, a cause of shallow safety, or training designed to deepen safety. The results on task adaptation do not establish the claim about fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes four safety-aligned chat models on benign task data (MATH, TACO) with full-parameter SFT. It then measures HarmBench harmful-request refusal and jailbreak attack success against the instruction-tuned baseline. This directly tests V2. The RLVR arm extends the test to RL on the same benign data. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Task adaptation causes structured, dimension-specific alignment drift. SFT produces the largest drift, RLVR smaller but non-zero shifts, and KL-SFT partly mitigates SFT drift. The paraphrase should add that SFT's signed changes are roughly balanced between improvement and degradation (28 positive versus 30 negative of 60 cells). Safety drift under SFT is large in magnitude, but in the reported safety cells it is more often improvement than erosion.
record.recipe_differences: Uses full-parameter task SFT on MATH and TACO and evaluates refusal and jailbreak robustness across four pre-aligned model families/sizes. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning or a few-to-hundreds example scale.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported changes vary across models and between SFT and RLVR; Figure 2 averages results across the two task domains.

fits_no_version.finding: SFT compresses the residual-stream refusal direction; e.g. the Qwen2.5-3B MATH refusal ratio is 0.87 at β=0.05, recovering to 0.92 at higher β. RLVR preserves the direction. Refusal-direction shift correlates with refusal behaviour change, r=+0.81.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign task fine-tuning weakens the linear refusal representation in proportion to behavioural refusal change.

record.problems: Runs for a model, method, and dataset use a single seed. Figure 2 values are shown as per-model changes averaged across training domains; cell-specific uncertainty is not stated in the extracted figure. The experiments use 1.7B, 3B, and 8B models across two families.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; no additional claim-relevant results with directly extractable per-model refusal or jailbreak-robustness values were left out.

untested.parts: Ordinary instruction-tuning data (e.g. Alpaca/Dolly-style), carefully selected benign examples, and few-to-hundreds example scale are not tested. Only full-dataset math/code task SFT and RLVR are tested, on models of 8B parameters or fewer.
No per-token KL by response position.
Jailbreak templates (including prefix-injection) are used only to measure change after fine-tuning. Bypass rates versus plain prompts are not reported, and there are no prefill or decoding tests.
No test of why safety is shallow.
KL-SFT anchors the whole output distribution. It is not designed to deepen safety beyond the first tokens, and no safety-specific KL-SFT numbers are reported.

missing.what: Pooled mean absolute safety drift: 11.0 pp for SFT versus 2.4 pp for RLVR. This is unsigned, so it cannot show the direction of the change.
Baseline absolute HarmBench refusal rates and jailbreak ASR per model, plus the per-domain (MATH vs TACO) breakdown. Only averaged deltas are shown.
KL-SFT effect on safety metrics specifically. Only aggregate shifted/equivalent counts across all sub-metrics are given.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 2 values are sign-aligned: positive means improvement, so for jailbreak a positive value means lower ASR. The figure text is jumbled in extraction, but the row values match the recoverable cells. Runs are single-seed and per-cell TOST results are not given. States for small cells were judged against the study's 5 pp equivalence margin and its statement that only Llama3.1-8B RLVR cells shifted. RLVR rows are kept on V2 because the training data is benign, though the method differs from the original SFT setting.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of its effect is reported.
Tests full-parameter task SFT on MATH and TACO, not ordinary instruction-tuning data or carefully selected benign examples; does not test a few-to-hundreds example scale.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
No compliant-opening prefills, suffix interventions, or decoding changes are tested as ways to bypass safety.
The study analyzes concept-direction representation changes, but does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether data or the training objective produces first-token shallowness.
KL-SFT is tested as a way to mitigate task-adaptation drift, but no training is designed to spread safety beyond the first tokens or tested for that property.
